newsitem.title: USA: Kansas winter wheat condition improving.
newsitem.headline: Kansas winter wheat condition improving.

text.p: Kansas winter wheat received snow and rain in February and is ready to break dormancy in mostly good to excellent condition, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"The crop appears to have received little damage during the winter from freeze and wind," the service said in its monthly winter crop report. "The western one-third of Kansas received a good snow cover during late February and potential blowing problems were diminished."
Winter wheat condition was rated 17 percent excellent, 62 good, 18 fair and only three percent poor.
That compared with last month's rating of 10 percent excellent, 65 good, 22 fair and three poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated 27 percent surplus, 66 adequate and seven short. That compared to last month's rating of three percent surplus, 67 adequate, 26 short and four very short.
Some areas of central, south central, east central and southeast Kansas have surplus moisture and field activity has been limited, the report said.
Livestock feeding conditions have generally been good, although mud has been a problem in some areas.
